learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will accurately differentiate between phrases and clauses, understand dependent and independent clauses, and identify noun, adjective, and adverb phrases.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Think of grammar like building with Lego blocks. A single word is a small block. Put a few together, and you get a 'Phrase' block. Add a subject and a verb, and it upgrades to a 'Clause' block! Let's learn how to snap these pieces together to build complex sentences.

lesson_modules.module_title: 🧩 What is a Phrase? (वाक्यांश क्या है?)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: A phrase is a group of words that makes some sense, but not complete sense. Crucially, it DOES NOT have a Subject and a Verb working together. It acts as a single part of speech in a sentence.

lesson_modules.module_title: ⚙️ What is a Clause? (उपवाक्य क्या है?)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: A clause is a group of words that DOES have a Subject and a Verb. Some clauses can stand alone as complete sentences (Independent/Main Clauses). Others depend on the rest of the sentence to make sense (Dependent/Subordinate Clauses).
examples_or_templates: Independent: **I ate an apple** because I was hungry.
Dependent: I ate an apple **because I was hungry**. (It can't stand alone as a full sentence)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Phrases are named after the job they do. A Noun Phrase does the work of a noun. An Adjective Phrase describes a noun. An Adverb Phrase modifies a verb.
examples_or_templates: Noun Phrase: I love **playing cricket in the rain**.
Adjective Phrase: A boy **with blue eyes** walked in.
Adverb Phrase: He fought **in a brave manner**.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Is the bolded part a Phrase or a Clause? 'She was waiting **at the bus stop**.'
❓ Identify the Dependent Clause: 'We will go to the park if it stops raining.'
options: We will go to the park

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Replace the bold Adjective Phrase with a single Adjective: 'A crown **made of gold**.'
subjective_practice.hint: What do we call something made of gold? A ______ crown.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Identify the Independent Clause in this sentence: 'Although he was tired, he finished his project.'
subjective_practice.hint: Which part of the sentence makes complete sense completely on its own?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Tell whether the bold group of words is a Noun Phrase or an Adverb Phrase: 'He answered the question **with great intelligence**.'
subjective_practice.hint: It tells us *how* he answered the question.

activity_or_assignment.title: ✂️ The Sentence Surgeon
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down a long sentence from your favorite book. Using three different colored pencils, underline a Phrase in green, an Independent Clause in blue, and a Dependent Clause in red!

chapter_summary: ⭐ A Phrase is a group of words without a subject-verb pair (e.g., in the corner).
⭐ A Clause is a group of words with a subject and a verb (e.g., when the sun rises).
⭐ Clauses can be Independent (can stand alone) or Dependent (need the main sentence to make sense).
